rounds.proof_sketch: outer_idx = blockIdx.y ∈ [0, outer_size-1]. Grid is configured with grid.y = outer_size. The mutation changes >= to >, but since max(outer_idx) = outer_size-1, both conditions 'outer_size-1 >= outer_size' and 'outer_size-1 > outer_size' evaluate to false. The boundary case outer_idx == outer_size is never reachable.
rounds.survival_reason: The CUDA grid is launched with grid dimensions (grid_x, outer_size). CUDA guarantees blockIdx.y ranges from 0 to grid.y-1, meaning outer_idx ranges from 0 to outer_size-1. The mutation changes the boundary check from >= to >, which only differs when outer_idx equals outer_size. Since outer_idx can never equal outer_size (it maxes out at outer_size-1), both the original and mutated conditions always evaluate identically (to false) for all valid thread indices. This is an architectural constraint of CUDA, independent of input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation affects a boundary check for outer_idx >= outer_size vs outer_idx > outer_size, but CUDA grid launch semantics prevent outer_idx from ever equaling outer_size. No input values can change this architectural constraint.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should incorporate CUDA-specific semantic analysis to detect when boundary mutations in index checks are unreachable due to grid/block dimension constraints. The condition outer_idx >= outer_size is redundant defensive code since outer_idx < outer_size is guaranteed by the grid configuration.
